newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada looking "hard" at Clyde bid.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada looking "hard" at Clyde bid.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Monday it was "taking a real real good look" at its bid for Britian's Clyde Petroleum Plc, but stopped short of confirming a report that said it would rais the bid on Tuesday.
"We're taking a real good look at our bid and whether that means considering raising it or considering leaving it is your interpretation," Gulf Canada spokesman John Sparks said in an interview.
"We're going to make sure that the number on the table tomorrow is the one we won't second guess or regret."

Sparks made the comment in response to a report in London's Daily Telegraph newspaper which said Gulf was expected on Tuesday to raise its offer for Clyde to 120 pence ($1.92) per share from the current 105 pence ($1.68).

"Gulf is considering whether its offer is adequate but I don't know about the number. I don't imagine Gulf is going to do anything until the opening of business in Britain or just before the market opens," he said.
Calgary-based Gulf Canada launched its offer for Clyde in December in a deal that is currently valued at 432 pounds ($692.6 million. A 120 pence bid would boost the value to $792 million.
The deal is seen by Gulf as its "third leg on the stool," or start of operations in a major basin to complement oil and gas exploration and production in Canada and Indonesia.
